document.title: Inventory Project Product and Engineering Framework

requirements.statement: This PDF is the governing product and engineering baseline after Product Owner approval.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Signed approval page and controlled document hash.

requirements.statement: Gaurav Mehta is Product Owner and sole approval authority for v1.0.
DBA and Operations feedback is retained as technical review evidence without separate approval authority.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Review evidence listed in the change record.

requirements.statement: No release or application change proceeds while this framework is unapproved.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Release ledger contains no post-freeze production package.

requirements.statement: Every change starts with a requirement ID or approved change request.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Change request links to affected requirement IDs.

requirements.statement: Direct production edits, minified JavaScript patches, manual database corrections, and reused migration IDs are prohibited.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Repository and deployment evidence show packaged, unique, reviewed changes.

requirements.statement: The approved framework remains effective for five years unless amended through change control.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Document control records approval and amendment history.

requirements.statement: Source is committed and tagged before any implementation candidate is releasable.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Git commit, clean status, signed or protected tag.

requirements.statement: Production request path is Browser -> IIS -> compiled React -> Fastify /api/v1 -> PostgreSQL.
IIS owns public port 80; Fastify binds 127.0.0.1:3020; PostgreSQL binds 127.0.0.1:5432.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Port and service inspection after reboot.

requirements.statement: Vite, gateway, presentation mode, memory persistence, direct browser database access, and runtime schema creation are prohibited in production.
React presents server state and never defines permissions, validation, statuses, fields, or report semantics.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Source conformance tests and API-driven rendering tests.

requirements.statement: Fastify owns authorization, validation, transactions, concurrency, and stable response contracts.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Endpoint tests under every role and failure mode.

requirements.statement: PostgreSQL is authoritative for inventory, configuration, permissions, imports, reporting definitions, and activity.
Snipe-IT and InvenTree are architectural references, not copied code or user interface.
Dependencies and responsibility boundaries are recorded and owned.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Operations dependency inventory and owner matrix.

requirements.statement: API and web compatibility are exposed by a version contract and checked before publication.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Version endpoint and updater compatibility check.

requirements.statement: One locked component system governs all product pages and cosmetic changes.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Visual regression suite and token audit.

requirements.statement: Application objects reside in dedicated PostgreSQL schema invmgmt after one controlled migration from public.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Schema inventory, object ownership, grants, and migration evidence.

requirements.statement: Database inventory_project and schema invmgmt are distinct concepts; PostgreSQL remains the only database engine.
Every relational business record has a primary key and every relationship uses a foreign key.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Catalog query finds no missing required key.

requirements.statement: Display labels are not stored as relational identifiers.
Physical deletion of referenced business records is prohibited; assets archive and configuration deactivates or deprecates.
Business foreign keys use RESTRICT unless an approved lifecycle rule explicitly permits another behavior.
Technical children use CASCADE only when their parent is the sole owner of their lifecycle.
Serial number is required and globally unique; populated asset tag is unique.
Exactly 19 standard fields exist: eight required and eleven optional.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Registry count assertion and generated surface tests.

requirements.statement: Lifecycle statuses are exactly IN_USE, REWORK, E_WASTE, ARCHIVE, GPU_READY, and AVAILABLE until changed through governance.
Locations follow Building -> Lab/Room -> Rack -> RU -> Cabinet/Storage with nullable optional assignment.
Indexes support identifiers, status, model, location, owner, date, references, activity, and resumable imports.
All business mutations are atomic, revision-controlled, permission-checked, and recorded in Activity.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Rollback, conflict, authorization, and activity tests.

requirements.statement: Migrations are immutable, unique, transactional, forward-only, and executed before application startup.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Migration ledger and failure rollback tests.

requirements.statement: Database ownership and grants follow least privilege; PUBLIC cannot create application objects in invmgmt.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Role, schema owner, and privilege catalogue.

requirements.statement: The profile registry is the only source of field behavior.
A field definition includes key, label, definition, help text, type, validation, uniqueness, aliases, visibility, ordering, active state, and deprecation state.
Profile versions pin import sessions and preserve historical interpretation.
Administrator field additions propagate to Add, Update, Filter, Detail, Import, Report, and Export without code changes.
Field keys are immutable after first use; labels may change with audit.
Invalid destructive profile changes with active dependencies are blocked clearly.
Dropdown values have aliases, active state, ordering, usage count, and ownership.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Admin lookup registry and import matching tests.

requirements.statement: Optional blank controlled fields never produce validation errors.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Create, update, filter, and import tests.

requirements.statement: Storage mappings are explicit and checked for compatibility with field type.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Registry health query and admin validation.

requirements.statement: Every enabled surface declares how it consumes each enabled field.
Phase 1 uses a database-backed company-network user picker without passwords or SSO.
Every listed member receives User; Igor Margulis, Monica Martin, and Gaurav Mehta also receive Super User and Privileged Administrator.
The backend resolves actor, roles, and permissions from the session; clients cannot submit or spoof them.
User may view assets, history, and print labels.
Super User adds and updates assets, operates assets, imports, exports, views reports and activity, and resolves permitted lookup issues.
Privileged Administrator manages profiles, lookups, locations, identities, roles, and system configuration.
Unauthorized operations return a structured 403 and are not merely hidden in React.
SSO is a later controlled phase and cannot be partially enabled in Phase 1.
Asset Model stores shared manufacturer, SKU, model, specifications, and image; Asset stores instance identity and state.
Create and Update are profile-driven and validate server-side.
User actions are Assign, Return, Transfer, Change Status, Archive, and Restore.
requirements.requiredEvidence: UI terminology and operation endpoint tests.

requirements.statement: Assign, Return, Transfer, status, archive, and restore update state and Activity in one transaction.
Asset updates require revision and stale edits return structured 409 Conflict.
Relationships use explicit parent, child, and relationship type and prevent self-reference.
Model images are type, size, and dimension validated and have category fallback icons.
NVBug, MRS, and Capacity references are relational, normalized, deduplicated, and preserved individually.
Multiple references accept comma, semicolon, or newline separators and return newest first.
Compact cards show the newest reference plus additional count; details show all reference groups.
Imports use persistent, resumable server-side sessions.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Leave, resume, restart, and ownership tests.

requirements.statement: Create Assets and Update Existing are separate modes; update matches exact unique Serial #.
Templates and instructions are generated from the pinned profile version.
CSV parsing supports UTF-8 BOM, quotes, commas, Windows endings, and multiple rows.
Mapping accepts case-insensitive labels, field keys, and configured aliases but never guesses ambiguity.
Duplicate headers, duplicate mappings, and unmapped required fields block validation.
Validation classes are Valid, Warning, Blocking Error, and Configuration Error.
Required blanks block; optional blanks, including Location, do not block.
Unknown required Owner or Vendor blocks; unknown optional Location warns and imports without location.
Optional free-text Notes is never validated as a controlled value.
Controlled values resolve by exact value, normalized value, and active alias.
Every issue links to row and field and offers correction, approved value, authorized add, source correction, or profile repair as applicable.
Users may edit, bulk-correct, and export validation issues without re-uploading; every source row must be corrected before import and cannot be skipped.
Included rows commit atomically and idempotently; any database or conflict error rolls back the batch.
Successful commit refreshes Search, Inventory, Reports, Activity, import history, and category totals.
Report calculations execute server-side and are registry-driven.
KPI, drilldown, and CSV export share one filtered query contract and reconcile exactly.
Reports include totals, lifecycle availability, category, status, location, owner, vendor, model, and project breakdowns.
Reports include missing metadata, rework, e-waste, aging, and date-received trends.
Every KPI and chart element opens its matching paginated asset result.
Report responses always initialize KPI, dimensions, trends, rows, and pagination.
Saved reports store owner, filters, columns, sorting, and compatible profile version.
CSV export is generated by the server with permission and Activity records.
Charts provide text/table equivalents and do not use color alone.
No report may label incomplete or stale data as current without a visible qualification.
Activity is immutable and records actor, time, action, source, reason, record type, and record ID.
Activity records parent import/bulk operation and NVBug/reference context where applicable.
Before/after changes are structured rows, not embedded in narrative reason text.
Every activity response initializes changes as an array.
Every event links directly to the affected asset, profile, import, or admin record.
Global and asset activity are paginated and filterable.
Create, update, status, assignment, transfer, import, profile, lookup, image, export, and print actions are covered.
Malformed or legacy activity data cannot blank the Activity route.
All public application endpoints are versioned under /api/v1.
Collections return arrays even when empty; optional aggregate objects are initialized.
Errors use a stable envelope with status, code, message, details, requestId, and latest conflict state when relevant.
Pagination uses documented page, limit, total, and deterministic ordering.
Asset responses always include nvbugs, mrsOrders, and capacityRequests arrays.
Import create, fetch, validate, correct, and commit return one documented session envelope.
Version endpoint exposes web, API, schema, import-contract, and package compatibility.
Request IDs appear in logs and user-visible failure states.
The frontend normalizes responses before rendering and rejects incompatible contracts visibly.
API catalogue and frontend requests reconcile with no undocumented call.
The component system defines typography, spacing, fields, buttons, cards, tabs, sheets, dialogs, tables, and feedback.
Pages use professional domain wording and do not expose implementation terminology to users.
Every page has loading, empty, permission, configuration, and failure states.
Route-level error boundaries prevent one malformed record from blanking a route and offer Retry and Return to Search.
Overlays have one internal scroll surface, fixed actions, backdrop/Escape/close dismissal, and focus restoration.
Browser Back closes overlays or returns to the prior page without losing committed state.
Search text, category shortcuts, and applied filters remain independent.
The NVIDIA logo is official, clickable, and returns to Search while clearing transient state.
Motion is restrained, communicates state, and respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Supported widths have no overlap, clipped actions, nested scrollbars, or horizontal page overflow.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Screenshot and overflow suite at five required viewports.

requirements.statement: Forms expose definitions, required state, constraints, and direct recovery guidance without clutter.
Labels use Code 128 SVG, isolate print content, create one label-sized page per asset, and record print activity.
Production runtime is IIS, one Fastify Windows service, and PostgreSQL; Node runtime is bundled.
Start order is PostgreSQL, Fastify, then IIS; stop order is IIS, Fastify, then PostgreSQL when database maintenance requires it.
Operations provide install, migrate, start, stop, restart, status, maintenance, logs, cleanup, and health commands.
Normal changes use component deltas; full baseline is only for clean installation or disaster recovery.
Delta updater verifies version and hashes before stopping services and publishes only declared components.
Temporary packages and temporary previous components are removed after success; no persistent backup or snapshot is created by this framework.
Maintenance mode protects users during component switch and never masks a failed recovery.
Logs are structured, rotate, contain request IDs and record links, and separate service, update, audit, and health concerns.
Health includes liveness, readiness, version compatibility, database reachability, and dependency state.
External monitoring alerts on unavailability, sustained latency, error rate, and database connection failure.
Support documentation defines ownership, severity, diagnosis, escalation, and recovery.
A release ledger records version, package hash, operator, components, migrations, acceptance evidence, and outcome.
Requirement IDs appear in automated test names and the generated conformance report.
HTTP 200 alone cannot approve a release; browser rendering and business workflows are mandatory.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Acceptance report includes browser and workflow gates.

requirements.statement: Every route is tested directly and through navigation under all three roles.
Database tests cover keys, constraints, indexes, rollback, restart persistence, ownership, and deletion behavior.
Five concurrent sessions cannot silently overwrite asset changes.
Import tests cover all 19 fields and one administrator-added twentieth field.
Report KPI, drilldown, and export reconcile for every standard dimension.
Visual acceptance covers 1920x1080, 1366x768, 1280x720, 768x1024, and 390x844.
Performance targets are p95 <500 ms search/detail, <800 ms mutation, and <2 s reports at expected volume.
requirements.requiredEvidence: Load report with five concurrent sessions.

requirements.statement: A candidate with any failed applicable requirement is not packaged or assigned a release version.

standardFields.label: MRS order #
standardFields.definition: Material Request System order reference. Canonical header and key accepted; configured aliases may extend mapping.

standardFields.label: NVBugs #
standardFields.definition: Internal NVIDIA bug, enhancement, or task reference. Normalize, deduplicate, and preserve individually.

standardFields.label: Date Received
standardFields.definition: Day 0 receipt date. ISO date in API; locale-friendly display in UI.

standardFields.label: Board SKU
standardFields.definition: Board or card assembly code shared by the asset model.

standardFields.label: GPU SKU
standardFields.definition: GPU or chip variant code shared by the asset model.

standardFields.label: Model #
standardFields.definition: Manufacturer or internal model identifier used to resolve shared model metadata.

standardFields.label: Serial #
standardFields.definition: Unique physical or logical instance identifier. Exact match key for Update Existing import mode.

standardFields.label: Milestone
standardFields.definition: Engineering checkpoint or maturity state associated with the asset instance.

standardFields.label: Product Name
standardFields.definition: Human-readable product name shared by the asset model.

standardFields.label: Location
standardFields.definition: Foreign key to the hierarchical location tree. Blank never blocks import.

standardFields.label: Status
standardFields.definition: Lifecycle status from the approved six-value status list.

standardFields.label: Board Architecture
standardFields.definition: Approved architecture classification. Blank is valid; aliases are registry-managed.

standardFields.label: Pool/Team
standardFields.definition: Organizational pool or team responsible for operational use. Blank is valid.

standardFields.label: Project
standardFields.definition: Project or operational activity associated with the asset.

standardFields.label: Asset Tag #
standardFields.definition: Organization-issued asset identifier. Blank allowed; populated values unique.

standardFields.label: Owner / Assignee
standardFields.definition: Foreign key to the selected application user responsible for the asset.

standardFields.label: Notes
standardFields.definition: Free text up to the configured limit. Never treated as a controlled value.

standardFields.label: Vendor
standardFields.definition: Foreign key to the approved vendor record.
